name: AIO (weekly 24-hr infusion 5-FU/LV)

drugs.name: Leucovorin
drugs.notes: Source (DeVita 12th ed., line 123467, citing Kohne et al., 1998): 'LV 500 mg/m2 over 2 hr, followed by 5-FU 2,600 mg/m2 over 24 hr, repeated weekly.' Weekly regimen; day shown as 1 of each 7-day cycle.

drugs.name: 5-Fluorouracil
drugs.notes: Source (DeVita 12th ed., line 123472, citing Kohne et al., 1998): '5-FU 2,600 mg/m2 over 24 hr, repeated weekly', given immediately after the leucovorin infusion. Weekly regimen; day shown as 1 of each 7-day cycle.

premedications.name: Antiemetic prophylaxis
premedications.notes: per low emetic risk tier, see supportiveCare

supportiveCare: Antiemetics: low emetic risk tier (5-FU/leucovorin, per NCCN Antiemesis guideline categories, Appendix D) - prophylaxis for 10-30% emesis frequency

G-CSF: not routinely indicated; AIO weekly 5-FU/LV is not a high or intermediate febrile-neutropenia-risk regimen per NCCN Appendix C categories - physician discretion if patient-specific risk factors present

monitoring: renal function (dose adjustment context for 5-FU/LV regimens)

doseModificationRules.text: Review required. Protocol-specific delay/reduce criteria may apply; physician decides.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: Cancer of the Colon, Table 40.11; lines 123467 (leucovorin), 123472 (5-fluorouracil). Setting/stage/intent from the same chapter's 'Management of Unresectable Metastatic Disease' section (lines 123342 to 123347, 123352), which contains Table 40.11.
